title: Juvenile in conflict with law - when is a minor tried as an adult
p1:
A child commits a serious crime. Does the law always treat that child like an adult?

The answer may surprise many people.
p2: A common misconception is that every person below 18 is automatically tried only through the juvenile system. In India, the law allows a special process for certain children between 16 and 18 years accused of serious offences.
p3:
If the alleged offence falls under the category of a heinous offence, the Juvenile Justice Board first conducts a preliminary assessment. It looks at factors like the child's mental and physical capacity, ability to understand consequences, and the circumstances of the offence. Only after this assessment can the matter move forward for trial as an adult in certain cases.

The key point: age alone does not decide everything. The nature of the offence and a careful legal assessment also matter.
conclusion: Do you think the law should allow minors accused of serious offences to be tried as adults in some situations? Share your views.
